title: Naturality of the unbounded exchange morphism
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square and $\Lambda$
a commutative ring. For every morphism $\varphi:K\to K'$ in
$D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
g^{-1}Rf_*K&\xrightarrow{\ \Ex_{\square,K}\ }&Rf'_*g'^{-1}K\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle g^{-1}Rf_*(\varphi)}&&
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle Rf'_*g'^{-1}(\varphi)}\\
g^{-1}Rf_*K'&\xrightarrow{\ \Ex_{\square,K'}\ }&Rf'_*g'^{-1}K'
\end{array}
$$

commutes; that is, $K\mapsto\Ex_{\square,K}$ is natural in $K$.

proof.text:
Use the unbounded module functors and derived adjunctions of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Write $F=f^{-1}$, $R=Rf_*$, $F'=f'^{-1}$, $R'=Rf'_*$, $G=g^{-1}$, $H=g'^{-1}$, $U=GR$ and $V=R'H$, with composition read from right to left. Write $\theta:F'G\xrightarrow{\sim}HF$ for its natural derived square comparison. For an object $K$ put $a_K=\eta_{f',UK}$, $b_K=R'(\theta_{RK})$, and $c_K=R'H(\varepsilon_{f,K})$. The explicit defining formula is $\Ex_{\square,K}=c_K\circ b_K\circ a_K$. For $\varphi:K\to K'$, naturality of the adjunction unit at $U\varphi$ gives
$$R'F'(U\varphi)\circ a_K=a_{K'}\circ U\varphi.$$
This is the defining naturality identity for the unit, with its source and target evaluated at $UK$ and $UK'$.

proof.text:
Apply naturality of the natural isomorphism $\theta$ in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] to $R\varphi:RK\to RK'$. It says $HF(R\varphi)\circ\theta_{RK}=\theta_{RK'}\circ F'G(R\varphi)$. Apply the functor $R'$ to this equality and use preservation of composition. Since $G(R\varphi)=U\varphi$, the result is
$$R'HF(R\varphi)\circ b_K=b_{K'}\circ R'F'(U\varphi).$$

source.place: Proof, final sentence: naturality of the mate; explicit constituent calculation, step 2

proof.text:
For the adjunction $F\dashv R$ provided by [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], the counit's defining naturality identity at $\varphi$ is $\varphi\circ\varepsilon_{f,K}=\varepsilon_{f,K'}\circ FR(\varphi)$. Apply the functors $H$ and $R'$ and use their preservation of composition. With the notation of step 1 this is
$$V\varphi\circ c_K=c_{K'}\circ R'HF(R\varphi).$$

source.place: Proof, final sentence: naturality of the mate; explicit constituent calculation, step 3

proof.text:
Substitute the three equalities of steps 1--3 into the explicit exchange formula of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], using associativity:
$$\begin{aligned}
V\varphi\circ\Ex_{\square,K}
&=V\varphi\circ c_K\circ b_K\circ a_K\\
&=c_{K'}\circ R'HF(R\varphi)\circ b_K\circ a_K\\
&=c_{K'}\circ b_{K'}\circ R'F'(U\varphi)\circ a_K\\
&=c_{K'}\circ b_{K'}\circ a_{K'}\circ U\varphi\\
&=\Ex_{\square,K'}\circ U\varphi.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $U\varphi=g^{-1}Rf_*(\varphi)$ and $V\varphi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}(\varphi)$, so this is exactly commutativity of the displayed square.
